key_insight: The minimum perturbation energy needed to trigger turbulence in pipe flow decreases as Re^-3, even though the optimal disturbance shape changes only by becoming thinner and more localized with increasing Reynolds number.
engineering_relevance: This scaling helps predict transition thresholds for pipeline and internal-flow designs, enabling more reliable control strategies and lower-margin stability assessments at high Reynolds numbers.
method: Variational optimization of nonlinear perturbations to laminar pipe flow for Re <= 5000
Track how optimal structures evolve with Reynolds number, including Orr growth, oblique-wave interaction, and lift-up
Measure how perturbation thickness and energy gain scale across phases
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computed optimal perturbations up to Re 5000 and finds consistent scaling laws: thickness ~ Re^-1/3, Orr-phase gain ~ Re, nonlinear stages ~ Re^2, and transition at a constant energy threshold leading to minimal energy ~ Re^-3.
watch_item: The results are based on computed optimal perturbations over a finite Reynolds-number range, so extrapolating the Re^-3 law to much higher Re or different pipe conditions should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Scaling of the minimal energy for turbulence transition in pipe flow
